# PR Agent decision record

Scope: the review bot added in `.github/workflows/pr-agent.yml` and
`.pr_agent.toml`. Mode: **Full** (network, credentials, multiple components).

Everything below is tagged:

- `[VERIFIED: source]` — read from an official doc, shipped config, or source.
- `[MEASURED: how]` — observed in a run on 2026-11-07.
- `[UNVERIFIABLE]` — no source; treat as an open risk.

## Components

GitHub Actions workflow, pr-agent 0.49.0 (Docker action), LiteLLM (inside
pr-agent), Command Code Provider API, model `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`,
repository secret, `.pr_agent.toml` policy.

| D28 | Agent state CLI | `scripts/review-state.sh` | Reads the `pr-agent-review-state:v1` typed block: head staleness, coverage, finding counts, `path:line`; TOON-ish output, exit codes, `--help`, `--version`; `--gate` for the verdict and `--reviewed` for whether another run is worth a model call. Without a typed block the head is read in this order and no other: the guide header, then the persistent review line naming the commit, then a bare `commit/<sha>` in the body. The last is only a resort, because a review that discusses an earlier fix quotes one, and a body link must never outrank a head a run recorded (finding `3de53d74d7e9`) | `[VERIFIED: review comment state block; scripts/check-review-gate.sh body-link-does-not-beat-recorded-head]` |
| D29 | Coverage gate | `.github/workflows/review-gate.yml` + `review-state.sh --gate` | 3 of 12 sampled merged PRs had no review comment (#92, #83, #82, all force-pushed); the review bot has no `synchronize` trigger. The trigger is the review run, not the comment: the bot posts with `GITHUB_TOKEN` and GitHub starts no workflow for events that token creates, so an `issue_comment` trigger never fires for it (`workflow_run` on `PR Agent` does). That is the only trigger: a `pull_request` one would execute the PR's own copy of the workflow, which is the copy it is judged by. The gate fails on a missing, stale or incomplete review and on any verdict other than `No concerns found` (`REVIEW_GATE_VERDICT` overrides it), runs only the default branch's copy of the script, never the PR head's and never the PR's base ref, so a PR aimed at another branch cannot choose the script that judges it, and makes no model call, so it spends no credits. Only the bot's own comment counts (`REVIEW_BOT_LOGIN`, default `github-actions[bot],github-actions`), and it must carry the typed block; the guide header is not enough, because `/describe` prints it too: the marker text alone is forgeable by any commenter, and the looser `Risk level` alternation let a newer `/describe` comment shadow the review. Before it lands the check does not run at all: `workflow_run` fires only for a workflow that exists on the default branch. A base without `--gate` fails loudly rather than passing, because a neutral result counts as a pass.  | `[MEASURED: 100 pr-agent runs, 55 success; 3/12 merged PRs with zero comments, 2026-11-17; review round on #99 found the red-gate and forgeable-comment holes, 14/14 cases after]` |
| D30 | Usage telemetry | `output_run_details = true`; pr-agent `0.50.0-github_action` | Tokens and duration were unobservable: the job log prints prompt tokens only, so a cost claim had no source. 0.50.0 renders model, tokens in/out/total, prompt cache, duration, and AI calls on the review comment, which is the record the gate and the decision table can cite. `output_run_cost` stays off because litellm has no price for this model id and would print "unavailable" on every review | `[VERIFIED: pr_agent/algo/run_output.py show_run_details @ 0.50.0; Docker Hub digest 548e894a...]` |
| D31 | Push coverage | `pr-agent.yml` trigger `synchronize` + `github_action_config.handle_push_trigger` with `push_commands = ["/review"]` + a reviewed-SHA skip step that runs `review-state.sh --reviewed --sha <pushed sha>` | #115: a head that received a commit after the PR opened got no review at all and nothing said so; #112 rebased, listed six checks, none of them a review, and merged. A pushed commit is what a merge decides on, so it needs a review of its own; the earlier "one review per PR" decision (N9) was written for a surface that judged the PR, not the commit. The trigger is only half of it: with `handle_push_trigger` off, the action logs `Skipping action: synchronize`, exits 0, and reviews nothing — a green run that proves nothing (run 44461713521). Three bounds keep it from becoming a model call per push: the job guard skips drafts and forks, the action itself skips merge commits and a bot's push, and a head that already carries a complete review of that exact commit skips the model step. The skip reuses the gate's predicate (`--reviewed`) instead of a second definition of "reviewed", and an error in it reads as "not reviewed", so a broken check costs a model call rather than silently leaving the head unreviewed | `[MEASURED: #112 rollup: six checks, no review, merged CLEAN, 2026-11-18; run 44461713521 "Skipping action: synchronize", 2026-11-19]`; `[VERIFIED: github_action_runner.py @ 0.50.0 lines 385-425; scripts/check-review-gate.sh --reviewed cases]` |
| D32 | Head-anchored verdict | `review-gate.yml`: resolve the PR head once, judge it with `review-state.sh --gate --sha <head>`, and write the verdict onto that commit with the Checks API (`checks: write`) | Measured, and it settles where a gate check can go: a `workflow_run`-triggered workflow runs on the default branch, and its own check is attached to the default branch's HEAD, not to the commit the review run checked out. So the gate's own check can never gate a PR head — that is why #112 had six checks and no `Review` — and it must never fail on a review verdict, which would leave a red `Review Gate` on `main` outliving the PR it described (#111, run 44247662200). The verdict is written onto the PR head instead: a push run writes it for the head it reviewed, a `/review` run (which checks out the default branch but reviewed the PR) writes it for the head too, and a push run whose head moved on reports nothing, because that head has its own run. That is what N13 rejected as unreachable and N14 named as the prerequisite for requiring the check: a check anchored on a pushed head once can never be revised, but one written onto the head by every later `/review` can | `[MEASURED: 20/20 `Review Gate` runs listed `headBranch: main` on 2026-11-19, including run 44461071558 whose `workflow_run.head_sha` was PR #132's head 5ca51d0, whose `Resolve` step passed and whose `gh pr checks` at that head listed 7 checks and no `Review Gate`]`; `[VERIFIED: scripts/gate-review-selfcheck.sh 9/9]` |
| D33 | State block | `pr-agent.yml` appends `<!-- pr-agent-review-state:v1 … -->` to the guide comment after the container posts | The pinned image emits no block on a clean review (#140), so `review-state.sh` read `present: false` and the gate reported "no review comment from the bot" about a review that ran. The image cannot be patched, so the workflow appends the shape the gate awk-parses: the marker line, one JSON line, `-->` alone. The head comes from the body's own `Review updated until commit` footer, else the event payload; there is no API read, because that answers the head at append time rather than the one the review read, so a push in between would be recorded as reviewed (#153), a merge recommendation must be present or nothing is written, only a comment authored by `github-actions[bot]` is touched, selection stops at the newest bot review (blocked or not, never falling back to an older one), and a body that already carries a block is never rewritten. The comment list is read with `--paginate`, so a PR past one page still offers its newest review, and the step repeats the job's draft and fork guard, so a draft cannot be written to if the job guard ever changes. `findings` stays `[]` because the container publishes no typed findings, so `--findings` cannot read detail out of an appended block; the verdict still comes from the body, which is where the gate reads it | `[MEASURED: PR #148 guide comment 7004549373, 752 chars, "No concerns found", no marker line, 2026-11-19]`; `[VERIFIED: scripts/check-pr-agent-state-block.sh 14/14, including the real gate returning gate: pass on the body the step wrote]` |
| D33a | Ledger deleted | A ledger comment recording each judged head (`<!-- review-gate-ledger:v1 head=… block=… complete=… verdict=… -->`, posted before the verdict was written, never edited), and the first-run bound it carried, are both gone: the ledger is deleted, not fixed. `review-gate.yml` posts no comment (its `pull-requests` permission is back to `read`), `review-state.sh` prints no `ledger:` line, and `prior_blocks` reads only the comments that exist now. What replaced the bound is the same statement without a mechanism: the gate detects a vanished block only while an older block survives beside the new comment | Two findings on the ledger's own implementation, and both are structural to where it wrote. It was appended by the gate after the gate had already decided, so the first review of a PR had no row when the gate read it; and the line printed before the `present` check, so every failed gate run — no review, stale review, non-clean verdict — posted another comment on the PR. Repairing both means moving the write into the review run and making it idempotent, which is a second mechanism to keep correct. Deleting it removes the comment surface, the race, and the claim; the bound it was protecting is stated in AGENTS.md "Agent review surface" and in the comment above `prior_blocks` instead of being implied by a row, and that bound does not depend on a first gate run happening at the right moment | `[VERIFIED: rg -n 'review-gate-ledger' sources/review-state.sh/check-review-gate.sh/gate-review-selfcheck.sh/review-gate.yml -> zero hits; scripts/check-review-gate.sh 54/54; scripts/gate-review-selfcheck.sh 9/9]` |
| D33b | Header regex | The guide header's head is `commit/<40 lowercase hex>` after the phrase, with the span bounded to the URL (`https://[^ )]*commit/`) and the closing paren optional | The pattern allowed anything but `)` between the phrase and the link. A truncated or reformatted header has no closing paren, so the span ran to the end of the line and backtracked to the last `commit/<sha>` on it — an older fix the header quotes, read as the head. Bounded to the URL, the only link it can reach is the header's own, so the first link after the phrase wins by construction rather than by the fixture happening to put it last. A short sha is not accepted: the template writes all 40 | `[VERIFIED: scripts/check-review-gate.sh truncated-header-and-prose-guide-marker; reverting the pattern or the marker anchor to the f54084d forms fails exactly that case]` |
| D33c | This file is review input, bounded | `.pr_agent.toml` `repo_context_files` is `AGENTS.md`, `NEXT.md`, `context.md`; `.github/PR-AGENT.md` is now added to it, still bounded by `repo_context_max_lines = 900` against 1,285 lines across those four files | A bound documented only here is invisible to the reviewer, so it is re-filed as a fresh finding on the next review — which is how the ledger row and the header pattern each came back twice, resolved and then re-raised. An accepted bound must be stated in `AGENTS.md` or a code comment, which is where these two now are. This file is the decision log and now also reviewer input, which is the point of the add: a bound only the log records is one the reviewer never reads. The line cap is why the addendum cannot be assumed to load, so a bound that must bind is also stated in `AGENTS.md` or a code comment (finding b835ca937d10: the row said the file was not review input while the same row added it to `repo_context_files`) | `[VERIFIED: .pr_agent.toml repo_context_files, repo_context_max_lines = 900; wc -l AGENTS.md NEXT.md context.md .github/PR-AGENT.md = 1,285]` |
| D34 | No record, no pass | `review-state.sh --gate` clears only a typed block that records `last_run.complete: true` and a `head_sha` that matches the judged head at seven or more hex characters, as a prefix in either direction, because a review may quote an abbreviated sha; the length floor is what stops a truncated or mistyped value from matching a head that merely starts the same way. A review with no block is `unrecorded`, and `unrecorded` fails. `--reviewed` answers the same question, so a block-less review is not reviewed and the push trigger re-runs it. A head may only come from a comment that is itself a review, both review kinds select one (`:full` and `:incremental`, finding 6488fe1fce59), that head is read in the selected review and no other (D36), and a marker inside a fenced or indented code block is a quote, not a marker (D35) | Finding `b312598ba745`: `unrecorded` was a bound, not a record — a truncated or timed-out run that still printed a clean recommendation and a guide header was indistinguishable from a clean review, and the gate passed it. The guide header can date a review; it cannot certify that its run finished, so it is read to name the failure and never to clear one. The same premise decides the other two: a non-review bot comment quoting the persistent review line could supply the head (finding `33acdf68e0d2`), and a review quoting a block in an example made the PR look like it had carried one (finding `f7d291ec6f97`). Two consequences are accepted knowingly: a zero-finding review carries no block, so it fails until a run records one, and that failure needs a run, which costs a model call because `--reviewed` no longer skips a review nobody recorded. The comparison is a prefix match and not equality, and stating it as equality was finding `13d53e61b390`: a review may quote an abbreviated sha, so seven characters or more match in either direction and the length floor is what stops a truncated value from matching a head that starts the same way | `[VERIFIED: scripts/check-review-gate.sh unrecorded-clean-does-not-pass, green, reviewed-unrecorded, fallback-head-from-non-review, fenced-block-is-not-a-prior-block, fenced-block-in-review-is-not-a-block, info-string-fence-is-not-a-block, pre-example-is-not-a-block, indented-block-in-review-is-not-a-block, prefix-head-is-current, short-head-is-not-current; reverting each guard fails exactly its case: 61/61]` |
| D35 | A quoted block is not a block | `defenced` drops all three shapes a review quotes a block in — a fence, with or without an info string (` ```json `, `~~~text`) or with text before the marker (`text ```html`); a `<pre>`/`<code>` example; and an indented code block (four spaces or a tab) — and the state block is extracted from that same filtered body (`body_q`), so the awk keeps only a marker at column 0, where a run writes one, and a `-->` to close. A quoted block is therefore neither read as that review's own block — it cannot supply `complete: true` — nor counted as a block the PR has carried. What stays a bound: a fence opener that does not end with the marker and its info string (text after the language, or a space between the two), because the leading-text rule is anchored to end of line; and a block quoted at column 0 with no wrapper at all, which is byte-for-byte what a run writes and is not distinguishable without trusting a producer we do not control | Finding `e6024f4c203c` has three parts, each measured: the awk skipped fences only and took the marker after any indentation, the helpers knew nothing of `<pre>`/`<code>`, and a fence opened as `text ```html` was not a fence at all — so a quoted block carrying `complete: true` and the judged head cleared the gate with no run recording one, and the same quote counted in `prior_blocks`, turning a clean review into `missing`. The earlier reading of this was to accept the bound, on the argument that indentation would have to be re-derived and a wrong guess would swallow the real block; the rules here are narrower than a guess — only lines starting with four spaces or a tab, only `<pre>`/`<code>` regions, and only an opener that ends the line — so the one thing they can still do is drop a real block when a review's prose ends in a triple-backtick code span, and a dropped block reads `unrecorded`, which fails | `[VERIFIED: scripts/review-state.sh defenced + body_q; scripts/check-review-gate.sh fenced-block-in-review-is-not-a-block, info-string-fence-is-not-a-block, leading-text-fence-is-not-a-block, pre-example-is-not-a-block, code-example-is-not-a-block, indented-block-in-review-is-not-a-block — each fails when its own rule is reverted to the ebf4437 form; fenced-block-is-not-a-prior-block, doc-bounds-are-recorded]` |
| D36 | The head is the selected review's own | `head_from` reads the persistent `Review updated until commit` line from the review that was selected and from no other comment, so an older review's line cannot name the head of the one being judged | Finding `bed8f31fda88`: `head_from` took the newest bot comment that is a review and carries the line, which is not the newest review. With the newest review naming no head, an older review's line supplied one and the gate reported `does not cover the head being judged` where the failure it means is that no run of this review recorded anything. The case it was protecting — the persistent line is the only record of a judged head — is the selected review's own line (`body-link-does-not-beat-recorded-head`), which this keeps: restricting the read to the selected comment drops the cross-comment fallback and nothing else | `[VERIFIED: scripts/check-review-gate.sh fallback-head-from-an-older-review, body-link-does-not-beat-recorded-head, fallback-head-from-non-review, persisted-line-odd; reverting `head_from` to the newest matching comment fails fallback-head-from-an-older-review]` |
| D37 | Block history is what survives | `prior_blocks` counts the block-bearing comments that exist now, and that is the whole of it: the review is one comment a run rewrites in place, so a run that rewrote it without the block erased the only evidence that a block had existed, and the count reads 0 where 1 is meant | Finding `aab48f179d5e`: the PR's stated invariant is that a PR which ever carried a block keeps one, and the code cannot enforce it for the in-place rewrite, because the only evidence was the comment the run overwrote. What it costs is a named repair, not a pass: with nothing recorded the absence reads `unrecorded` where `missing` is meant, and both fail the gate. A ledger of judged heads was built for this and deleted (D33a) because it raced the comment it described; the bound is stated rather than fixed because any evidence kept outside the review comment is a second source of truth the gate would then have to trust | `[VERIFIED: scripts/review-state.sh the `prior_blocks` comment names the limit; scripts/check-review-gate.sh doc-bounds-are-recorded fails when this row is deleted, missing-block-named-before-stale, block-vanished, block-vanished-current]` |

A force-pushed head's older check stays on the older commit, which no rollup reads, because checks are per-commit. | N7 | Auto-merge or auto-approve | Review is advisory; approval stays human | `[VERIFIED: enable_auto_approval default false]` |

## Coverage

| Component | Knobs covered | Knobs deliberately defaulted |
|---|---|---|
| Workflow | triggers, permissions, concurrency, guards, timeout, image pin, env | runner choice, retry of the job itself |
| pr-agent | model, fallback, custom_model_max_tokens, max_model_tokens, max_output_tokens, reasoning_effort, additional_reasoning_effort_models, ai_timeout, repo context, auto tools, response language | temperatures, seeds, callbacks, labels, score/effort sections |
| Provider API | base URL, endpoint, auth, model, reasoning effort | ZDR header, Responses API, Anthropic Messages |
| Secrets | name, scope, fork policy | environment-scoped secrets |
| Policy | reviewer/description/suggestion instructions, ignore rules via repo context | per-directory settings, global org settings |
| Everything else in `configuration.toml` | `[N/A]` — webhooks, callbacks/telemetry, vector DB, chat integrations, publishing cosmetics, OpenRouter controls, per-directory/global settings | Not reachable from this deployment |

Coverage script: `coverage_diff.py` against `configuration.toml` reported many
`GAP` rows for the `[N/A]` group above and `SINGLE-SOURCE` because only one
machine-readable source was supplied. Both are recorded here, not hidden. The
Provider API facts were checked against the live endpoint instead of a file.

## Agent experience (AX)

The surface is built agent-first: a coding agent reads the PR comment and acts;
a human reads it second. The contract lives in `AGENTS.md` under "Agent review
surface".

| Role | How it is served |
|---|---|
| Reader | `.github/PR-AGENT.md` is the reference; policy loads from `main`; repo context bounded at 900 lines |
| Developer | Inline file:line findings, typed risk and merge verdict, one persistent comment, deterministic `/review` and `/describe` commands |
| End user (agent) | Machine-readable state over prose; merge stays a human action; CI and Sim remain the gates |

Invariants applied:

- Typed contracts over prose: `require_risk_assessment`,
  `require_merge_recommendation`, `inline_key_issues`, and the
  `pr-agent-review-state:v1` block the bot embeds in its comment.
- State command: `scripts/review-state.sh` turns that block into compact state:
  head staleness, coverage, finding counts, and `path:line` rows.
- Recovery-shaped failures: a failed tool fails the check and posts a failure
  comment; it never turns green.
- Machine-readable state: one persistent comment with stable keys, not a thread
  an agent has to reconstruct.
- Trust boundary closed by default: rules and config from `main`, fork PRs
  skipped, commands limited to OWNER, MEMBER, COLLABORATOR.
- Prose guides, gates guarantee: the bot advises; CI and Sim enforce.

   `finish_reason=length` in the Action log. `[UNVERIFIABLE]` without a larger PR.

## Rollback

Delete `.github/workflows/pr-agent.yml`, `.pr_agent.toml`, and
`.github/PR-AGENT.md`; remove the `COMMAND_CODE_API_KEY` secret. No runtime
state, no deployed service, no data to clean up.
